minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to take a rephased Marshall Park plan to spring town meeting and let the skate park build through October 1, 2025.
minutes.summary: The commission, meeting in person in a small room without Zoom, spent most of the night on Marshall Park. It heard the interim Town Manager on ARPA deadlines, voted to proceed with a rephased plan, and held a long discussion with youth baseball and softball representatives about user fees and field maintenance. It also approved an RDLA invoice, the skate park access timeline, a May all-vendor fair date and four sets of minutes. User fees were put on the December agenda with no decision.

public_comment.speaker_as_heard: Greg Le frer, 15 Park Street Terrace
public_comment.topic: Asked where the projected 5-10 year maintenance plan for Marshall Park is, and who will maintain what once phases are complete. Youth baseball and softball have carried that burden so far.
Linked user fees to the cost of maintaining new facilities, which will cost more than the old fields to maintain.
Said youth baseball and softball brings over 5,000 visitors to the parks and asked for consideration and communication.
Said the user fee conversation came up when the field-use notification was voted on. Argued the commission should analyze maintenance across all parks, and asked about capital plans for other parks.
Said youth sports feel pushed out in town, with football, baseball and softball all affected. Asked for understanding of recreational sports.
Asked when field maintenance allocations will be known. Questioned whether Parks is responsible only for big design projects and who handles repairs.
Asked whether the schools pay to use the ball fields, whether pickleball users would be charged, and who handles toilets and trash.
Said the fields are already degraded and asked what backend plan accompanies any user fee increase. Questioned whether punch lists should go through Parks or the facilities director.
Asked that the town consider long-standing cultural groups such as youth baseball and softball, which bring many visitors. Said they feel brushed aside.
Asked why ARPA money is being returned to the town while the parks have many needs. The chair explained the funds were granted for this purpose and must be under contract by year end.

votes.motion: Authorize the recreation director to proceed with planning the all-vendor fair on May 10, 2025.
Move forward with the updated, rephased Marshall Park plan and a new request at town meeting in May.
Approve the RDLA invoice dated October 31.
Allow the skate park group to proceed with construction through October 1, 2025, without interrupting ball field use.
Approve the minutes of the four prior meetings as a group, with edits.

budget_items.what_was_said: The new estimate is far above the original anticipated cost and applies to phase one and the remaining work. There is not enough money for phase one now, so the fall special town meeting borrowing article was not pursued.
The design team estimates a range of funds is needed to bring phases 1 and 2 to permitting design with updated cost estimates before spring town meeting.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funds and amount to return to the town
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission holds ARPA funds. Using only part for design would leave a balance to return to the town for other departments before the calendar-year-end deadline.

The Town Manager said funds must be under contract or spent by December 31, so contingency estimates will not work. He said interest has accumulated on the funds and asked that firms submit bills by Tuesday to clear the account.

budget_items.topic: Public presentation and test pit observation costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The Town Manager said the proposals appear to omit in-person public meetings and observation of test pits. He estimated each meeting at a few thousand dollars.
The existing Skanska contract has enough authorized funds for the proposed work. The RDLA design contract will need to be amended.
The invoice covers design development, permitting and construction documents, and was approved for payment by motion.
The chair presented the current grounds maintenance contract by park. The facilities director thinks 17 mowings a year may be low.
Per-player fees were stated for in-town and non-resident players. Youth baseball paid a season total for its players, and the Phillies paid a smaller amount for out-of-town players.

budget_items.topic: School field fees paid by another league
budget_items.what_was_said: A speaker said a league pays a yearly sum to use school fields.
A design for a possible t-ball field at MCN is on the capital plan.
Capital projects must meet a minimum dollar threshold, whose value was uncertain. Smaller repairs fall to facilities day-to-day.
A speaker used a possible capital item as an example of something that could sit on the plan for years.

decisions.decision: The Marshall Park user fee discussion will move to the December agenda. No decision was made, and the chair wants the facilities director present.
The December meeting is likely December 18, location to be determined, with a bigger room sought.
The commission will ask the design firms to submit their bills by Tuesday, and the Town Manager will meet the chair to review concerns with the designer.
The skate park group is told it can build through October 1, 2025, with extension possible. The right-of-entry terms will be checked.
The chair reported the state was told the Parks Grant and the land and water conservation grant could not proceed. The state administrator encouraged reapplying and the commission intends to.
The chair will ask the minutes-taker to record motions, seconds and votes more specifically.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to move forward with a rephased Marshall Park plan and bring a new request to town meeting in May.
The commission voted to let the skate park group build through October 1, 2025, without interrupting ball field use.
A long discussion of Marshall Park user fees and field maintenance, with youth baseball and softball speakers, ended with no decision and a referral to the December agenda.
The commission approved an RDLA design invoice and authorized planning for an all-vendor fair on May 10, 2025.
The chair reported the state was told two grants could not proceed, and the commission intends to reapply.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park work now depends on a new funding request at spring town meeting, which residents would be asked to vote on, because the new estimate exceeded what was available for the first phase.
Any user fee for youth baseball and softball is undecided and will return in December, so fees and who pays for field upkeep remain open for residents who use the parks.
watch_next: The December Parks Commission meeting, likely December 18, where Marshall Park user fees return with the facilities director present.
The December 31 deadline for ARPA funds to be under contract or spent, and the May town meeting request.
